messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw a noisy tenant drive KV residency upward on gpunode-12 during longctx chat sessions. +6GB over ~30m, other tenants dropped to soft-evict frequently.
maya: Yikes. Any pprof traces?
sam: Pprof attached in thread (snippet below). Main oddity: pagewalks spike coincident with sequence-length tailups in batching. Noticed more slab fragmentation when kernel selection picks the int8 path vs fp16.
rob: Wait kernel selection affects slab fragmentation? how? :thinking:
sam: Short version: int8 kernels do denser packing but use a slightly different memalign+alloc path for KV pages in our runtime -> smaller page slabs and higher boundary slack. Longctx patterns that keep touching many unique keys cause more small-frag pages to be retained.
toni: Can you paste the profiling lines?
sam: Sure — pprof heap top lines (sanitized):
```
heap_profile: total 18.9GB
 3.2GB  kv_page_obj (hot)  -> repeated touch pattern
 2.7GB  slab_fragmentation_fragment (meta)
 1.9GB  prefix_cache_kv
pagewalks/sec: 14k -> bursts to 120k during the incident
```
maya: 120k pagewalks/sec is huge. Does this align to our kernel choice telemetry?
sam: Yes — correlates with a canary model rollout where scheduler started preferring an int8 variant for that tenant (cheaper FLOPs). Took a while to realize because model-level telemetry was tagged differently from tenant routing.
rob: So cheaper kernel -> more memory fragmentation -> more pagewalks -> eviction pressure -> noisy neighbor. That's a nasty chain.
toni: Any quick mitigation we can flip? Per-tenant soft quota exists but it's too blunt. Maybe a decay-based residency cap: decay per-key score if it's not touched within x secs, or penalize tenants whose pagewalk/sec exceeds threshold.
maya: I like penalizing pagewalk rate + reuse-frequency. If a tenant has high touched_pages but low reuse ratio (many cold touches), throttle its longctx retention.
sam: Reproducer I used locally to trigger it:
```bash
# synthetic longctx churner
for i in {1..10000}; do 
  curl -s -XPOST "$REDWOOD_API/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -d '{"model":"canary-int8","prompt":"<long history with unique keys>$i","max_tokens":1}' &
 done
wait
```
Gives same fragmented growth in 10-20 minutes on a small node.
rob: Good repro. Can we add a runtime guard: if pagewalks spike >50k and free_kv_memory < 10% then temporarily route new longctx sessions for that tenant to fallback (fp16) or lower retention policy?
toni: Yes, fallback routing by policy is doable and fast. Also propose: add a background compaction pass that merges adjacent small slabs when node is <80% load. Cheap and might reduce fragmentation without evictions.
maya: Also need better alerting: current SLO only tracks tail latency and token cost. Add a KV-residency growth alert and pagewalk/sec alert pinned to node + tenant.
ci-bot: deploy check: kv-residency-alert rule expanded to include pagewalk_rate > 50k and tenant_residency_growth > 2GB/30m. PR: https://ci/repo/changes/4821 :heavy_check_mark:
sam: Next steps I can own: 1) add the alert PR, 2) prototype fallback routing rule, 3) run compaction experiment on staging. Will post timelines by EOD.
maya: Thanks. If you need someone to triage canary traffic or look at model routing tags, ping me.
rob: I can take the compaction prototype once you have the baseline perf numbers.
toni: I'll draft the eviction-penalty heuristic doc (short spec) and post later today.
sam: Cool — logging notes saved in the incident artifact: `s3://redwood-debug/kv-frag/3126001234/` :eyes:
maya: :thumbsup:
